title: ACES: Accelerating Sparse Matrix Multiplication with Adaptive Execution Flow and Concurrency-Aware Cache Optimizations
problem: Sparse matrix-matrix multiplication (SpMM) involves massive irregular memory accesses that challenge cache-based architectures. Current SpMM accelerators struggle to adapt to diverse sparse patterns, fully exploit parallelism, and optimize cache performance.
motivation: SpMM is a critical computational kernel in scientific computing and machine learning applications.
method: ACES features an adaptive execution flow that dynamically adjusts to sparse patterns while balancing parallel efficiency and data reuse. It incorporates concurrency-aware cache management policies that co-optimize data locality and concurrency for replacement decisions. A non-blocking buffer is integrated with the global cache to enhance concurrency and reduce stalls. The hardware architecture cohesively integrates these mechanisms to support adaptive execution, cache optimizations, and fine-grained parallelism.
key_novelty: Concurrency-aware cache management policy that co-optimizes data locality and concurrency for sparse matrix multiplication.
contributions: Adaptive execution flow mechanism for handling diverse sparse patterns
Concurrency-aware cache management policy with locality-concurrency co-optimization
Non-blocking buffer integrated with global cache to enhance concurrency and reduce stalls
Hardware architecture achieving 2.1× speedup over existing SpMM accelerators
primary_theme: Adaptive sparse matrix acceleration with concurrency-aware cache optimization
